reason: Same behaviour: without a getter the lookup that follows is `WeakMap.get(undefined)`, which returns undefined as the short circuit does.

Performance only: a property the getter reads twice is recorded twice with the same value, because the snapshot is frozen and its getters are memoized. The later check compares that value twice and reaches the same answer.

Performance only: with nothing remembered as read, a property the getter reads twice is recorded twice with the same value, because the snapshot is frozen and its getters are memoized. The later check compares that value twice and reaches the same answer.
Same behaviour: the key comes from `Object.getOwnPropertySymbols` of the plain snapshot object built a moment before, so its descriptor is always there and the condition is always true.
Same behaviour: a descriptor without `value` belongs to an accessor, whose `descriptor.value` is undefined, so the type check that follows rejects it as well.

Same behaviour: this is `configurable` of a getter installed on the snapshot. Each key is installed once, and `Object.freeze(snap)` makes every property non-configurable before the snapshot leaves `createSnapshotRecursive`.

Same behaviour: this is `configurable` of a data field copied to the snapshot. No field is defined a second time, and `Object.freeze(snap)` makes every property non-configurable before the snapshot is returned.
Same behaviour: this is `writable` of a data field copied to the snapshot. Nothing writes the field again, and `Object.freeze(snap)` makes every property read-only before the snapshot is returned.

No effect: a finished node is in the snapshot cache at its current version, so a second visit in the same pass returns from the cache before `inProgress` is read, and the set is dropped when the pass ends. Only code that writes to the store in the middle of a snapshot, from a trap of a state object that is itself a Proxy, could reach the check.
